column1: # npm-scripts-allow.tsv — the npm scripts in this directory that are in NO gate
# tier, each with the REASON it is not.
# ⚑ AN ALLOWLIST WITHOUT REASONS IS A LIST OF THINGS NOBODY HAS TO JUSTIFY, and
# that is how nine ungated scripts accumulated here by 2026-07-30 — ~7,600 LOC of
# one window's FRI work and the whole of Route B's o1js side, with no mechanism
# that went red when the tenth appeared. `check-mina-npm-coverage.sh` requires a
# reason of at least 20 characters, and reds on a row that names a script
# The bar for a row here is one of:
#   (a) it is PLUMBING every gated leg already runs (`build`), or the tier-0 gate
#       runs directly under another name (`typecheck`), or is an alias (`test`);
#   (b) it needs CREDENTIALS OR A NETWORK a gate must not have (`devnet:*`);
#   (c) it is a LIVE LANE'S work-in-progress — and then the row NAMES the lane
#       and the follow-up, so the allowlist is a to-do list rather than a

column2: PLUMBING. Every gated leg runs `npm run <leg>`, which runs `build` first, so a tsc failure reds every tier. Tier 0 also runs `npx tsc --noEmit` directly.
PLUMBING. The tier-0 gate runs `npx tsc --noEmit` itself rather than through npm, so this alias would be a second name for a check that already reds.
ALIAS for `gate`, which is the tier-1 leg `gate`. Gating both would run the same object twice and let the two names drift apart.
NEEDS DEVNET CREDENTIALS AND A FAUCET. Deploying or funding is an outward-facing irreversible act; a gate must not hold the credentials to perform one, and this one spends.
NEEDS DEVNET CREDENTIALS AND A NETWORK. Deploys `DreggAttestedGate` — an outward-facing irreversible act a gate must not be able to perform.
NEEDS DEVNET CREDENTIALS AND A NETWORK. Submits a transaction to a live chain.
NEEDS DEVNET KEYS. Deliberately ungated and stated so in check-mina-attestation.sh's header; the `merkle` subcommand it wraps IS gated, end to end, by the `probe` leg.
NEEDS A NETWORK. Reads a live chain, so it cannot have a deterministic verdict.

LIVE LANE 2026-07-30 (the proof-gated anchor lane). Its tier-0 half is an out-of-circuit table and belongs at tier 0; its tier-1 half compiles the gate and needs the emitted chain pins first. FOLLOW-UP: gate at tier 0 the moment the lane names its PASS line, and at tier 1 once `dregg-chain-pins.json` exists.

LIVE LANE 2026-07-30 (the proof-gated anchor lane). Reproduces the claim-carrying uniform plan and emits `dregg-chain-pins.json` from the compiled key list; it is report-only until those 131 keys exist and refuses a partial emit. FOLLOW-UP: gate at tier 0 with `head-anchor` -- its report half runs in seconds and its ratchet cross-check reds when the plan moves.

LIVE LANE 2026-07-30 (the Lean-emitted-circuit lane). It is the differential between `KimchiPoseidon2.permGen`'s emitted instruction stream and the hand-written `provablePermBounded`, and it CANNOT be gated until `src/generated/kimchi-poseidon2-w16.json` exists -- the emitter is `lake env lean --run EmitKimchiPoseidon2.lean` and lives in another tree, so a gate would red on a checkout that has not run it. FOLLOW-UP: gate at tier 0 the moment the artifact is committed (its [0]-[3] half is an out-of-circuit weld and KAT and runs in seconds), and at tier 1 with `rows` for the head-to-head row measurement.

LIVE LANE 2026-07-30 (the column-narrowing lane). It is an out-of-circuit census and unit-price re-derivation with no compile in it -- exactly the shape tier 0 is for -- and it refutes the `1,067 rows per opened value` literal two other documents ride on. FOLLOW-UP: gate at tier 0 alongside `cost-gate`, whose registered unit prices it consumes.

NEEDS TO RUN ON THE MACHINE THE ANSWER IS ABOUT. It asks whether `@o1js/native-<platform>-<arch>` installed HERE and whether the two backends agree on a verification key; a gate that ran it on one box would report a fact about that box. It is step 0 of `bridge/demo/mina-verifies-dregg.sh`, which is where it belongs. FOLLOW-UP: none -- gating it would be gating a hardware question.

LIVE LANE 2026-07-30 (the deploy-path lane). The VK-independent rehearsal of deploy -> accept -> refuse for `DreggHeadGate`, and the file that MEASURED why `head-anchor` at MINA_TIER=1 is red (its stand-in producer is maxProofsVerified=0 against a class that declares 1, and its two stand-ins share a key because o1js keys do not depend on a program NAME). FOLLOW-UP: gate at tier 1 as the head-gate family's representative compile-and-prove instance -- it is 55s on hbox with the native backend.

NEEDS DEVNET CREDENTIALS AND A NETWORK. Deploys the PROOF-GATED `DreggHeadGate` -- outward-facing and irreversible, and a gate must not hold the credentials to perform one. It refuses without `--broadcast` and exits 3 with its blockers named.
NEEDS DEVNET CREDENTIALS AND A NETWORK. Submits the `advanceHead` transaction that is PLACEHOLDER_CUTOVER's P4 trigger. Refuses without `--broadcast` and exits 3 with its blockers named.

LIVE LANE 2026-07-31 (the merge-tree lane). Measures `mu` = merge-prove / leaf-prove, the one ratio every tree estimate swings on, by proving a two-SelfProof node around the SHIPPING `assertMergeable`/`foldCompose` body. Ungated because its denominator is READ from `.fullchain/pasta-braid-*-measurement.json`, which a clean checkout does not have. FOLLOW-UP: gate at tier 2 with the other prove-time measurements once the fold chain has a driver that emits its own leaf sample.

LIVE LANE 2026-07-31 (the merge-tree lane). The merge node against real prove() calls: a 4-leaf tree, the identity, associativity, and FOUR attributing controls (adjacency, claim carry, count additivity, leaf list), then `DreggFoldGate` deploy-and-advance on a LocalBlockchain with its own uncounted control. Self-contained and ~4 minutes with the native backend. FOLLOW-UP: gate at tier 1 as the fold family's representative compile-and-prove instance -- it needs no artifacts and it is the file that would go red if o1js changed the arity rules this design is built on.
